The case for Free use: reasons not to use a Creative Commons -NC license

I read this article and there's a lot of thought that's gone into it.

I have a couple of comments.

With regard to music so many musicians have seen others get rich off their efforts while they got little or nothing they feel compelled to fight against this and they see NC as a way to do this. Actually this is an entirely separate issue, for the most part musicians got screwed because of bad contracts with greedy companies.

Also songwriters still receive songwriter royalties even if their work is CC-BY. It is only the licensing fees you are relinquishing and these are only large for established hits or standards that carry cachet with them into the reuse. Many companies will insist on purchasing a license in any case, even for CC-BY material, because they want every i dotted and don't want any surprises at the end of the production cycle. So using a CC-BY license can get your work used and heard and can possibly make it more likely that you will receive a licensing fee than without the free culture license.

The article above is more general than this but I see so many musicians counter productively adopting NC because they are so afraid some one else might make some money on their music. In fact the only way you will make any money on your music is if someone else makes money on your music. No man is an island.
